text: , also known as Ana Nzinga, is a Kongolese leader and Great Person in the Civilization games and a Nigerian leader in the Call to Power games.
Pacal II (23 March 603 – 28 August 683), also known as K'inich Janaab' Pakal, was the king of the Mayan city-state of Palenque. He leads the Maya in Civilization IV: Beyond the Sword.
Pachacuti (1410 AD – 1471 or 1472 AD) was the ninth Sapa Inca of the Kingdom of Cuzco, which he transformed into the Inca Empire. He leads the Inca in Civilization V.
Osorkon is a non-playable leader from the Gifts of the Nile scenario in Civilization VI. A reused Saladin, he leads the Libyans and has no leader ability.
is a Macedonian leader in the Call to Power games, the wife of Philip II of Macedon, and the mother of Alexander the Great.

Otto I (23 November 912 – 7 May 973), traditionally known as Otto the Great, or Otto of Saxony, was East Frankish king from 936 and Holy Roman Emperor from 962 until his death in 973. A reused , he leads the Germans in scenario in Civilization III: Conquests.

Phill Boucher is an American composer and sound designer. He is known for helping to compose the soundtrack for Civilization VI. In addition to his work on the Civilization games, Boucher has composed music for Fortnite, Masterminds, Uncharted 4: A Thief's End, and Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales.
is a Macedonian leader in the Call to Power games, the husband of Olympias, and the father of Alexander the Great.
Peter Wicks (born January 24) is an English voice actor who speaks West Country English. He provided the voice of Edward Teach in Civilization VII.
Pocatello (1815 – October 1884) was a Shoshone chieftain. He led the Shoshone tribe both in freedom, and on their reservation. He leads the Shoshone in Civilization V: Brave New World.
Qin Shi Huang (259 BC – 210 BC) was the first emperor of a unified China in 221 BC. He leads the Chinese in Civilization IV.
Ragnar Lodbrok (or Ragnar Lothbrok) was a semi-legendary Norse king. He leads the Vikings in Civilization IV: Warlords.
Ramesses II (c. 1303 BC – July or August 1213 BC) was the third Egyptian pharaoh of the Nineteenth Dynasty. He leads the Egyptians in Civilization IV: Warlords.
Ramkhamhaeng (1237 or 1247 AD – 1298 AD) was the third king of the Phra Ruang Dynasty, ruling the Sukhothai Kingdom. He leads the Siamese in Civilization V.

Ramesses II (c. 1303 BC – July or August 1213 BC) was the third Egyptian pharaoh of the Nineteenth Dynasty, reigning from 1279 BC to 1213 BC. He leads the Egyptians in Sid Meier's Civilization. Normal Aggression Normal Development Civilized Total threat level: 2 Musical Theme Inspiration: Harvest of the Nile (original composition)

Rafael Urdaneta is a Comandante General in Civilization VI. His unit provides +5 Combat Strength and +1 to land units within 2 s. Urdaneta can be retired to reset the movement and attacks of each of the player's land combat units within 2 tiles.

Rafael Kayanan (born September 13, 1962) is a Filipino American comics artist and Filipino martial arts master. He illustrated Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri: Power of the Mind Worms, a graphic novel based on Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri and its Alien Crossfire expansion. He has also illustrated numerous comic books and graphic novels for many publishers, including DC, Marvel, and Vertigo Comics.
Franklin D. Roosevelt (30 January 1882 – 12 April 1945) was the 32nd President of the United States. He leads the Americans in Civilization IV.

Rurik, also spelled Rorik, Riurik or Ryurik, (830s – 879) was a Varangian chieftain of the Rus' who, according to tradition, was invited to reign in Novgorod in the year 862. A reused , he leads the Kievan Rus' in scenario in Civilization III: Conquests.

Roger Briggs (born May 28, 1952) is an American composer, conductor, pianist, and educator. He is known for composing (or helping to compose) the soundtracks and prepare sound effects for Civilization III, Pirates!: Live the Life, and Civilization IV: Warlords. Briggs has a Doctorate in Music Composition from the Eastman School of Music.
Salah ad-Din Yusuf ibn Ayyub, or Saladin (c. 1138 – 4 March 1193), was the first Sultan of Egypt and Syria and founder of the Ayyubid dynasty. He leads the Arabs in Civilization IV.
Sakir-Har is a non-playable leader from the Gifts of the Nile scenario in Civilization VI. A reused Tomyris, he leads the Hyksos and has no leader ability.

Sarah Lynn (formerly Sarah Darney) is a video game producer and writer who currently works for Firaxis Games as a marketing manager. She served as the associate producer for Civilization VI and was also involved with quality assurance, production, and writing for Civilization V: Brave New World, Sid Meier's Civilization: Beyond Earth and its Rising Tide expansion, and Sid Meier's Starships. Lynn is the narrator for all How To and First Look videos in Civilization VI (except Leader Pass) and Civilization VII.

The Scarab is an Alien unit introduced to Sid Meier's Civilization: Beyond Earth in the Rising Tide expansion. It has lower than even a Wolf Beetle, making it the weakest alien in the game. * : 2 * : 6

Lalla Aisha bint Ali ibn Rashid al-Alami (c. 1491 – c. 1552), better known by her epithet Sayyida al Hurra ("the Noble Lady"), was a Moroccan noblewoman who ruled as governor of from 1515/1519 to 1542. In partnership with , she became the undisputed leader of the in the western Mediterranean, turning Tétouan into a feared privateering hub against the Spanish and Portuguese fleets. She is a leader in Civilization VII. She is available with the within the , which was released on December 9, 2025.
Shaka (c. 1787 – c. 22 September 1828) was the most influential leader of the Zulu kingdom. He leads the Zulus in Civilization IV: Warlords.
, also known as Sammuramat or Shamiram, is an Assyrian leader in the Call to Power games.

Tsar Simeon (also Symeon) I the Great (864/865 – 27 May 927) ruled over Bulgaria from 893 to 927, during the First Bulgarian Empire. Simeon's successful campaigns against the Byzantines, Magyars and Serbs led Bulgaria to its greatest territorial expansion ever, making it the most powerful state in contemporary Eastern and Southeast Europe. His reign was also a period of unmatched cultural prosperity and enlightenment later deemed the Golden Age of Bulgarian culture. A reused , he leads the s in scenario in Civilization III: Conquests.
Simon Burke (born October 8, 1961) is a voice actor who speaks Australian English. He provided the voice of John Curtin in Civilization VI.
Smoke-Jaguar was the 12th ruler of Copán. He was born in 612 A.D., became ruler in 628 A.D., and died in 695 A.D. He leads the Maya in Civilization III: Conquests.

Joseph Stalin (18 December 1878 – 5 March 1953) was a Georgian-born Soviet politician who became General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union. He leads the Russians in Civilization IV: Warlords.
Suleiman I (6 November 1494 – 7 September 1566) was the tenth Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1520 until his death. He leads the Ottomans in Civilization IV: Beyond the Sword.
Sweyn II is a playable leader from the 1066: Year of Viking Destiny scenario in Civilization V. A reused Harald Bluetooth, he leads the Danes.

Svein Forkbeard or Sweyn Forkbeard (17 April 963 – 3 February 1014) was King of Denmark from 986 until his death, King of England for five weeks from December 1013 until his death, and King of Norway from 999/1000 until 1013/14. A reused , he leads the Danes in scenario in Civilization III: Conquests.

Tekámthi (c. 1768 – October 5, 1813), commonly known by his name Tecumseh, was a Shawnee chief and warrior, best known for his efforts, alongside his brother , in promoting unity and resistance among Native Americans against the onto their land, forming a of tribes and joining the as a British ally until his death at the . He is a leader in Civilization VII. He is available as with the , released on February 11, 2025, simultaneously with the initial game release.
Te Arahi Napi Maipi is a voice actor who speaks Māori. He provided the voice of Kupe in Civilization VI: Gathering Storm, for which he was credited as TeArahi Napi Maipi.

Genghis Khan (c. 1162 – 18 August 1227), born Temüjin, was the first Great Khan of the Mongols, uniting the nomadic tribes of the Mongolian steppes under his rule and founding the Mongolian Empire, which after his death became the largest contiguous land empire in history. He leads the Mongols in Civilization III: Play the World.

Theodora or Θεοδώρα (c. 500 – 28 June 548) was the wife of Emperor Justinian I. She ruled over the Byzantine Empire, which (at its peak) ruled over most countries around the eastern Mediterranean. She leads the Byzantines in Civilization V: Gods & Kings.
, also known as Tigranes II, is a Armenian leader in the Call to Power games.

Tokugawa Ieyasu (31 January 1543 – 1 June 1616) was one of three unifiers of Japan, alongside Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Oda Nobunaga. After Hideyoshi's death, he founded the powerful Tokugawa Shogunate, which ruled peacefully for more than two hundred years. He leads the Japanese in Civilization IV.

Toyotomi Hideyoshi (16 February 1537 – 18 September 1598) was a Japanese and , considered one of the three great unifiers of Japan alongside Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu. Rising from a peasant background, he became the most powerful man in Japan, acquiring the prestigious titles of and and completing the of Japan started by his predecessor and liege lord Nobunaga. He is a leader in Civilization VII. He is available with the within the , which was released on June 22, 2026.

Trưng Trắc (c. 14 – c. 43) was a military leader who, alongside her sister Trưng Nhị, led a of Vietnamese tribes against the by the Han dynasty, reigning as for three years from 40 to 43 until their rebellion was defeated. She and her sister are still highly revered in Vietnamese culture, being considered national heroines and symbols of Vietnamese independence. She is a leader in Civilization VII.

Vijaya Wimalaratne is an Great General in Civilization VI. His unit provides +5 Combat Strength and +1 to Information era land units within 2 s. Vijaya Wimalaratne can be retired to grant a level and +100% combat experience to a military land unit.
Victor, otherwise known as The Castellan, is one of the s introduced in Civilization VI: Rise and Fall. He is the military governor who excels at defending cities from attacks. __TOC__
Wang Kŏn (31 January 877 – 4 July 943), also known as Taejo of Goryeo, was the founder of the Goryeo dynasty of Korea. He leads the Koreans in Civilization IV: Warlords.
, also known as Vlad III, is a Slavic leader in the Call to Power games.

William I (24 April 1533 – 10 July 1584), also known as Willem van Oranje, William of Orange, or William the Silent, was the main leader of Dutch revolts against the Spanish in the Eighty Years' War and the founder of the United Provinces in 1581. He leads the Dutch in Civilization V: Gods & Kings.

Wes Whitaker, known as "WesW" in the gaming community, is an American modder. He is known for creating a Medieval modpack for Civilization IV: Warlords, the Medieval Pack for Civilization: Call to Power, and the Medieval Pack for Call to Power II.
Wu Zetian (17 February 624 – 16 December 705) was the empress regnant of the Second Zhou Dynasty of the Chinese empire from 690 AD to 705 AD. She leads the Chinese in Civilization V.
Xerxes I was a Persian ruler who served as the fourth King of Kings of the Achaemenid Empire, reigning from 486 BC until his assassination in 465 BC. He leads the Persians in Civilization III.
Zara Yaqob (c. 1399 – June 1468) was emperor of Ethiopia (under the throne name of Constantine I) from 1434 until his death. He leads the Ethiopians in Civilization IV: Beyond the Sword.
, also known as Ögedei Khagan or Ogodei, is a Great Person in the Civilization games, the son of Genghis Khan and Bortei, and the uncle of Kublai Khan and Möngke Khan.
"Breaker" of the Ungodly is a Redguard member of The Ungodly residing at their camp at Sep's Spine, Alik'r.
"Slicer" of the Ungodly is a Redguard member of The Ungodly residing at their camp at Sep's Spine, Alik'r Desert.
"Shady" Syron is a Redguard outlaw. He is found at the docks near Murcien's Hamlet, which are used to travel to Blackheart Haven.

A'Tor was a Redguard who was the son of the last High King of Hammerfell, King Thassad II. Following his father's death, he led the Crowns against Baron Volag in the Hammerfell Civil War, but was mortally wounded by a poisoned arrow during the Battle of Hunding Bay.

Abhuki is a Khajiit, and the keeper of the Faregyl Inn and a Journeyman Alteration trainer. She will rent a bed for 10 a night. She can also help with the Master Alteration Training Quest, because she is an advanced Alteration trainer. After reaching Level 70 in Alteration, she will point to Tooth-in-the-Sea for further training.

Ababael Timsar-Dadisun is a Dunmer trader living in the Zainab Camp in the Grazelands. Ababael is a member of the Ashlanders faction, and resides in his yurt. Ababael is also the author of The Buying Game.
Abanji is a Khajiit slave who resides in Molag Mar, in the Molag Amur region. She has no unique dialogue and does not offer any services.
Abishpulu Shand is a Dunmer Farmer who resides at his hut near the city of Gnisis, in the West Gash region.

Abbard the Wild is a Nord Barbarian found near the ruins of Bal Fell, in the Azura's Coast region. He is a hireling of House Telvanni and is camped out with a group of Telvanni mercenaries: Edril Vules, Roggvar Blue-Tooth and Hirnir. He can usually be found standing alone, presumably guarding the area.
Abelone is a Nord citizen in who works at the Windpeak Inn as a maid in the city of Dawnstar.
Abassel Asserbassalit is a Dunmer Barbarian, and is of Ashlander ethnicity. He resides in his yurt in Aidanat Camp, in the West Gash region.
Abibaal Assillariran is a Dunmer Archer who resides near Molag Mar, in the Molag Amur region.
Achel is a Redguard commoner who resides in the St. Olms Canton, Canal South-Three of Vivec City, in the Ascadian Isles region.
Abelle Chriditte is a Breton Master Trainer in Alchemy located in the Propylon Chamber of Valenvaryon, in the Ashlands region.

Abnur Tharn is father to Clivia Tharn, the Empress Regent of Cyrodiil. He is known as High Chancellor and Overlord of Nibenay, he is an original member of the Five Companions, and also the Imperial Battlemage of the Elder Council. Abnur is 164 years old and has at least 16 children.
Abal at-Inzil is a Redguard priest of Tava on the island of Stros M'Kai.
Abdahel is a Redguard residing in the city of Port Hunding, Stros M'Kai. He is typically found talking to Meleril about various topics.
Abzag the Monster is an Orsimer residing in Daggerfall, Glenumbra. He can be found inside The Rosy Lion inn for one of the quests in the Undaunted questline.
Aamela Rethandus is a Dunmer found inside the inn in Selfora. She is tending to those who were wounded in the attack on town.
Abel Mathis is a Breton residing in Alcaire Castle in the region of Stormhaven. He is located just inside the southern gates.
Aarela is a Dunmer member of the Mages Guild. She is the magister of their branch in Hissmir.
Ababael is one of the undead Kothringi inhabitants of Stillrise Village, in the region of Shadowfen.
Abadi is a Redguard found in Camp Tamrith, in the region of Rivenspire, High Rock.
Abal-jo is a Khajiit mage working for House Montclair. He is part of the boss trio encountered within the ruins of Erokii.
Abanal is a Redguard situated in The Sloshing Tankard, in the region of Rivenspire, High Rock. He resides in the city of Northpoint.
Abadusa is a Khajiit bard found playing at the Temple of the Crescent Moons in Khenarthi's Roost. She has no unique dialogue.
Abal the Defiler is a Redguard found at King's Rest in the Alik'r Desert.
Accalia is an Imperial captain and the leader of the bandit gang established in Fort Sphinxmoth. Him and his men are responsible for the raid of a nearby temple of Mara.
Abiznaz is a Khajiit merchant and part of the gang found inside the outlaws refuge underneath Sentinel.
Abazadar is a Redguard enchanter and a co-owner of The Gem & Flask shop in Belkarth, Craglorn.
Abbess Iraldine is a Breton member of the religious group found at the Abbey of the Eight in Cyrodiil, and at St. Pelin's Chapel in Evermore.
Abbot Durak is the Orsimer leader of the Spirit Wardens at Pariah Abbey, in the region of Stormhaven, High Rock. At different times, he may also be found at the town of Shinji's Scarp.
Abernura is a Khajiit chef. She sells her wares at her stall, Sup and Sup Well, at the Merchants' Stall of Narsis.
Abradih is a Breton merchant living in Davon's Watch in the region of Stonefalls. She is a merchant, but offers no mercantile options, and has no unique dialogue.
Abrar is a Redguard living in Sentinel in the Alik'r Desert region of Hammerfell.
Abuana is a Khajiit banker and a member of the Aldmeri Dominion. She is found at the Western Elsweyr Gate.
Achene Douare is a Breton member of Captain Currod's crew in Koeglin Village, Stormhaven. He can be found on The Tava's Bounty being treated by Tyrrya Doure. He has no unique dialogue.
Abomination of Hate is a named Scamp found in the cemetery of Grimfield, Betnikh.
Achaeraizur is a creature that appears in . They are located in the Vaults of Madness in Coldharbour.
Abzrolg is an Orsimer mage and scholar found in the Orsinium Mages Guild in the city of Orsinium. He is a member of the Mages Guild.
Abandarra-la is a Khajiit merchant. She sells her wares at the camp found at the base of Sorrow.
Absolon is an Altmer in who resides in Riverwatch, his lighthouse.
Abijoo-Anoo is an Argonian traveling merchant found on the roads of Shadowfen.
Abelle Gernand is a Breton residing inside her house in Kvatch.
Accalia Celatus is an Imperial alchemist residing in Evermore.
Abadarun is a Redguard innkeeper, proprietor of The Serpent and the Senche in Abah's Landing.
Abe is a pet Assassin Beetle of the Mages Guild, residing on a platform on the back of The Blasted Breton. It is the only domesticated Assassin Beetle in the game, and will not attack the Vestige.

Acanthia, Chosen of Nirn is the spriggan boss of Bloodmayne Cave in Cyrodiil. they are one of three bosses (the others being Ironlash and Razorback) needed to complete the delve and receive the Achievement Bloodmayne Cave Explorer. potentially drops the bow: Acanthia's Arm of Cyrodiil's Light; part of the Light of Cyrodiil set.
Abazbi is a Khajiit woodworker that resides in Rimmen in Northern Elsweyr. She can be found at the Baandari Bazaar at her stall, Five-Claw Whittling Company.
Abadurr is a Khajiit residing in Rimmen. He can be observed dancing energetically.

Aburzin is a Khajiit commoner residing in Rimmen. He advises not to travel south to Pellitine, which between the Knahaten Flu and various murderers and thieves has become an unsafe place. He appears to be doing training exercises with Sinud and Zabhi in Urania Barbula's House courtyard.
Ab'dul was the king of Riverhold from around 3E 389 to 3E 399.
Aangehheyv is a hostile character residing in Southern Elsweyr.
Abadai is a Redguard found with her partner Parriot Conele in Little Ozur's Camp, Reaper's March, in .
Abbot Andor Indoril is a Dunmer residing in Holamayan Monastery in Vvardenfell.

, chief god of the Nine Divines]] The Aedra (singular: Aedroth) are one of the two groups of immortals which took part in the creation of Mundus. Their name is from the old Aldmeric language, and translates roughly into "our ancestors," referring to their role as the progenitors of Mer and Men. To the majority of cultures on Tamriel, the Aedra are revered as gods. As Oblivion is the night sky on Tamriel, so the Aedra are considered by some to be the planets. The largest eight planets are considered by Imperial society to be the Divines, while the stars are the Magna Ge.

Adrian Decanius is an Imperial commoner who lives in the Elven Gardens District of the Imperial City. He is one of the guards that works for Umbacano. He is often found at his house, or in the Arboretum.
Adrienne Berene is a Breton mage who lives in the city in Skingrad. She is the head of the local Mages Guild hall there, although she is not very well liked by those who work under her.

Aelwin Merowald is a Breton commoner and an old fisherman living in the two-building settlement of Weye, just outside of the Imperial City and right across the Wawnet Inn. He was working on his last job assignment before retirement, when he became crippled by a Rumare Slaughterfish he was trying to catch for its scales to sell to an alchemist. Aelwin is rather disgruntled and is sensitive to ridicule.

Aengvir is a Bosmer commoner living in the small town of Harlun's Watch, southeast of Cheydinhal. He can be found inside his house during the evening. He is well-respected locally, and is considered the unofficial mayor of the small town. Aengvir spends the majority of his time farming on his small plot of farmland where he grows several crops of cabbages. He also walks around and converses with the other citizens of Harlun's Watch and with travelers who happen to pass through the small village.
Adraria Vandacia is an Imperial agent and tax lady of the Census and Excise in Seyda Neen, in the Bitter Coast region.

Aengoth the Jeweler is a Bosmer scout who resides in the cellar of the The Rat in the Pot inn in the city of Ald'ruhn, in the Ashlands region. He is a Mastermind of the Thieves Guild and is the leader of operations at the Ald'ruhn chapter.
Addammus is a Dunmer Hunter who resides at his yurt in Ahemmusa Camp, in the Azura's Coast region.

Ada'Soom Dir-Kamal, also known as The King Among Demons, was a Kamal general and the leader of his race for a period of time during the Second Era. He was responsible for the Akaviri invasion of both Skyrim and Morrowind.

Adamus Phillida's Bodyguard is an Imperial guard who is assigned to protect Adamus Phillida after retiring from a successful career in the Imperial Legion, to the city of Leyawiin. He was given a bodyguard to ensure nothing bad would happen during his retirement. The bodyguard follows Phillida around, not actually having to do anything until an assassin from the Dark Brotherhood is hired to kill Phillida. Because the bodyguard failed his duty to protect Phillida and deemed himself a failure, he committed suicide. His body can be found inside the Leyawiin City Watch Barracks, along with a suicide note.
The Adoring Fan is a young and cheerful Bosmer commoner and a part of the "reward" for becoming Grand Champion in the Arena.

Adanja is a Khajiit pilgrim who resides in her home in Pelagiad, in the Ascadian Isles region. She has an interest in poisons, as the only two books in her home are about the subject. Adanja is not involved in any quests.
Aebondeius Jucanis is an Imperial Warrior who resides in the Dren Plantation, in the Ascadian Isles region. He serves House Hlaalu as an Oathman.
Adrianne Avenicci is an Imperial blacksmith who owns and operates Warmaiden's in Whiterun. She is the wife and business partner of Ulfberth War-Bear.

Acolyte Jenssen is a Nord Priest residing at the Temple of Kynareth in Whiterun. He is typically found in or around the temple all day. He is typically found standing over the bed of the Sickly Farmer performing healing spells, hammering the walls of the temple, or standing idly within it.
Adisla is a Nord farmer in who resides at Hlaalu Farm, east of Windhelm.
Addvar is a Nord fisherman and stall vendor in who resides at his house in Solitude. During the day, he is typically found selling items at his market stall, promoting his fish and other meats.

Adara is a Redguard child residing at Endon's House in Markarth. She is the daughter of Endon and Kerah and the sister of Cade, and is typically found within her house, with her mother at the market, or following her father around the city during the day.
Adeo is a Dark Seducer captain in charge of retaking Pinnacle Rock from the Knights of Order, minions of the Daedric Prince Jyggalag.
Adeber is a Breton miner who both works and resides at the Left Hand Mine, near the city of Markarth.
Adrimk was an Atmoran warrior and war-teacher who lived in the Merethic Era. She was one of the Five Hundred Companions.

Adairan Lalansour is a Dunmer Scout, and Ashlander. He is one of the bandits who have taken Beden Giladren hostage at Manat's Yurt in the West Gash region. Adairan wields an iron longsword and wears netch leather armor.
Adaves Therayn is a Dunmer pauper who resides in the St. Olms Canton of Vivec City, in the Ascadian Isles region.

Addarnat Assardidairan is a Dunmer scout who resides in a camp, in the Ashlands region, at location (6, -9). He is with Mut Urshan-Adairan and Manu Odirnapal, and all three will attack the Nerevarine on sight.
Adibael Hainnabibi is a Dunmer Ashlander Scout who resides in his yurt in the Kaushtababi Camp, in the Azura's Coast region.
Adil Norvayn is a Dunmer bandit warrior who resides in the cave of Kumarahaz, in the Azura's Coast region. Adil, as well as the rest of those in the cave, will attack the Nerevarine on sight.
Adosi Darano is a Dunmer thief who resides in the cave of Surirulk, in the Sheogorad region. He is hostile towards the Nerevarine.
Adrusu Rothrano is a Dunmer pilgrim and member of the Tribunal Temple who resides at the Canon Offices in the Temple Canton of Vivec City, in the Ascadian Isles region.
Aduri Sarethi is a Dunmer farmer in who lives at the Sarethi Farm with her sister, Avrusa.
Adharanji is a Khajiit slave who resides in the cave of Kudanat, in the West Gash region.

Aditte Oges is a deceased Breton spellsword whose body can be found in Shishi, in the Ashlands region. She is found dead in the ruins, presumably killed by the Guards inside. She was a member of House Telvanni.
Addvild is a Nord farmer in who resides at the Snow-Shod Farm with his wife, Leonara Arius. He will buy leeks, potatoes, and wheat from the Dragonborn.

Addhiranirr is a Khajiit thief, Thieves Guild member and connoisseur of the Vvardenfell's Black Market who resides in the St. Olms Underworks of Vivec City, in the Ascadian Isles region. She hides from a Census and Excise agent, and she is one of three sources of information during the Nerevarine's investigation of the Sixth House.

Adusamsi Assurnarairan is a Dunmer priestess who is being held as a slave at the Rotheran Arena, in the Sheogorad region. She offers skill training in a few magic disciplines if freed from her captors. There is only one opportunity to retain her services before she makes her escape, never to be seen again.
The Addict is a deceased Nord found inside Redwater Den. She presumably died of an overdose of Redwater Skooma. She possesses nothing other than a roughspun tunic and footwraps.
Aeradan is the Bosmer Camoran king of the Wood Elves. He is responsible for appointing Treethanes to administer different territories and settlements within Valenwood.
Adibazzi is a Khajiit trader who wanders the roads in the region of Grahtwood.
Adalabar is a Redguard hunter who resides in the Alik'r Desert, a region of the province of Hammerfell.

Aera Earth-Turner is a Nord brewer who initially resides in Bleakrock Village. She is mother of Trynhild and Littrek, and wife of Denskar Earth-Turner. She is forced to flee with the other inhabitants to Morrowind after the village was attacked by the Daggerfall Covenant. She later joins the Ebonheart Pact and is encountered a few times afterward at various places across Morrowind and Skyrim, such as Ebonheart, where she is inconsolable. Note that she can be found regardless of choice during Crossroads, as she was not an active participant in either quest.
Adjold is a Nord pack merchant residing in Davon's Watch in the region of Stonefalls. He runs a stall called Genuine Auroch-Hide Bags in the Market District of the city.
Adelle Montagne is a Breton residing in Aldcroft, Glenumbra. She is a member of the Mages Guild.
Admiral Rolston is a Breton mage and test character. He can only be met via the test cell ToddTest, using the console command COC ToddTest.
Advisor Norion is an Altmer member of the Veiled Heritance who resides in the Auridon city of Vulkhel Guard.
Adaishir is a Khajiit merchant. He sells his wares at his stall, Adaishir's Trustworthy Goods, at the Tree-Ring Trading Circle in Woodhearth.
Adabibi is a Khajiit patron of the Five Claws Inn in Woodhearth.
Adusharu is a Khajiit found at the Altmer embassy in Elden Root.
Ade the Southerner is a Nord tailor. He sells his wares at his stall, Serious Stitchery, at the stalls of the Redfur Trading Post.
Adamir is a Bosmer member of the Mages Guild residing in Marbruk, Greenshade.
Adiel Charnis is a Breton residing with her husband Arcady Charnis, in Dreughside outside Wayrest in Stormhaven.
Adlugbuk is an Orsimer found in Riften, in the province of Skyrim.
Aemilia Hadrianus is an Imperial residing in Cropsford. She is angered by Chef Amadour keeping a pet goblin, whom she suspects will cause trouble in the future.
Adele Barbe is a Breton merchant working at the Trader's Delight stall in the Craglorn city of Belkarth.
Admunayil is an Altmer residing in the city of Hallin's Stand.
Adras Teryon is a Dunmer laborer residing in the city of Ebonheart, Stonefalls.
Acolyte Sethrin is a Dunmer priest residing in the city of Ebonheart. He can be found in the Tribunal Temple.
Acolyte Vuri is a Dunmer priestess residing in the city of Ebonheart. She can be found in the Tribunal Temple.
Acolyte Indririi is a Dunmer priest residing in the city of Ebonheart.

Adept Izjadi is a Khajiit who appears in the Star Haven Adeptorium in Northern Elsweyr.

Adiah the Warbler is a Redguard gambler residing in The Stitches in Northern Elsweyr. She has no unique dialogue.
Aeliah Renmus is the half-Imperial, half-Redguard daughter of General Renmus.
Adifa Dunestrider is a Redguard guide hired by Lady Clarisse Laurent on her trip to Qharroa Ruins. She can be found sitting on the road in the northeastern side of the ruins.

Ah-Malz is an Argonian blademaster and member of the Fighters Guild in Skingrad. He is known around Skingrad for his hatred of goblins. When asked, he will recommend Derelict Mine as well as the whole West Weald for goblin hunting.

Ajum-Kajin is one of the Argonian mage ringleaders of the Blackwood Company in Leyawiin. He is found in Glademist Cave with some members trying to expand Blackwood Company's sphere of influence. Modryn Oreyn asks that Ajum be apprehended and interrogated so that he can learn exactly how strong the Company has become.

Agnorith Septim was the brother of Emperor Tiber Septim, the famed conqueror of a united Tamriel and the creator of the Septim Empire. He was the father of Kintyra Septim, who later became the Empress of the Empire after Pelagius Septim (Agnorith's grandnephew) died without any children. Every Emperor following Kintyra was a descendant of Agnorith's bloodline, up until the end of Cassynder Septim's reign. Very little is known about Agnorith aside from his family connections.
Aiden Direnni was a male Altmer Prince from the Direnni Clan of High Rock.

Agnar the Unwavering was a Nord warrior who was the chieftain of the village of Thirsk in Solstheim. His wife was Svenja Snow-Song, also a Nord who survived the Thirsk Mead Hall Massacre where the Udyrfrykte went on a destructive rampage and killed all of the patrons of the Thirsk Mead Hall except for her. Agnar became the chieftain of Thirsk after the Slayer of the Udyrfrykte. During the Oblivion Crisis, Agnar, through the questioning of researchers and adventurers, discovered that the Udyrfrykte was not the only one of its kind, but was only the offspring of a far greater beast known as the Uderfrykte Matron.
